text:
jordan: FYI customer on prod sees intermittent 401s after bundling our Node SDK with webpack. Started after bumping to 0.11.x.
priya: ugh, can you paste the error and a small repro? 401 from our API or from upstream?
jordan: api returns 401. customer sees header Authorization missing in downstream request. error snippet: 
```
Error: 401 Unauthorized
 at fetchWrapper (/app/node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/node/index.cjs:45:23)
 at Request.send (/app/node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/node/index.cjs:120:12)
```
jordan: their package.json exports looks like: "exports": {"./package.json": "./package.json","import": "./dist/esm/index.js","require": "./dist/node/index.cjs"} but they bundle with webpack and prefer `main`/`module` fields.
kevin: common issue: bundlers sometimes prefer the ESM build and then transform it causing dual fetch implementations or shim that strips Authorization on redirected or same-origin detection. also some bundlers rewrite conditional exports and end up pulling the wrong entry.
priya: can you share their webpack config? specifically resolve.mainFields and any rules around builtins/polyfills.
jordan: repro steps customer provided: 
1) npx create-react-app repro && cd repro
2) npm i @redwood/inference@0.11.0
3) in App.tsx: `import { createClient } from "@redwood/inference"; const c = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.REACT_APP_RW_KEY })`
4) npm run build; serve build -> calls to /v1 generate return 401

kevin: aha — CRA + webpack defaults to browser field -> pulls `dist/esm/index.js`. Our ESM build relies on `globalThis.fetch` polyfill behavior that some bundlers replace. If a polyfill lacks proper `Headers` propagation, Authorization header gets dropped. Another possibility: duplicated fetch packages (isomorphic-fetch) create two different Request prototypes so our header check fails.
priya: easy workaround for customer: force the CJS node entry during bundling by aliasing the package: 
```
// webpack.config.js
resolve: { alias: { '@redwood/inference$': require.resolve('@redwood/inference/dist/node/index.cjs') } }
```
that keeps the Authorization header intact.
sam: long-term fix: publish a dedicated browser ESM build that preserves header semantics, and update docs with bundler guide. also consider adding an `exports` subpath "./browser": "./dist/browser/index.js" so bundlers can pick explicit browser entry (and we test header behavior).
jordan: customer also reported types missing when they import `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference'` in TS after bundling — they get `createClient` as undefined at runtime.
kevin: that's packaging/exports map fallout. Some bundlers don't map `exports` correctly and TS resolves types from `types` in package.json but runtime picks a different file. that mismatch leads to undefined symbol. fix: ensure `types` path matches both exports conditions and add "types": "dist/index.d.ts" at top-level, plus an `exports` entry for `./package.json` pointing to package.json so tools can read it.
priya: can we reproduce locally quickly? jordan, can you drop a minimal repro zip in this thread and I'll run it. also please confirm node and webpack versions customer used.
jordan: sent repro link in DM. customer using node 18, webpack 5, CRA 5.
kevin: proposed patch in PR #987: - add explicit `./browser` and `./node` export conditions - ensure `types` aligns with exports - add a tiny runtime check that throws a better error if `Authorization` header isn't present so we can surface bundling issues instead of 401s downstream.
deploy-bot: release v0.11.1-rc1 deployed to internal npm tag `next` (sha: a1b2c3) · tests: bundler smoke · triggered by kevin
priya: assigned follow-up: kevin to finish PR + include docs snippet for webpack/rollup/parcel. jordan to coordinate with customer for temporary alias workaround. sam to add e2e for CRA build in CI.
jordan: thanks — keeping customer updated, will ping when they verify alias workaround works. :thumbsup:
